title: Sweet Is the Prayer Whose Holy Stream
description: Sweet Is the Prayer Whose Holy Stream in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 101, “Silent Prayer”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sweet is the prayer whose ho-ly stream In ear-nest plead-ing flows; De-vo-tion dwells up-on the theme, And warm and war-mer glows.

lines: Sweet is the prayer whose holy stream
Faith grasps the blessing she desires,
But sweeter far the still, small voice,
When God hath made the heart rejoice,
Nor accents flow, nor words ascend;

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
